headline.headline: HURRICANES ONE WIN FROM GLORY AS STAAL, CAROLINA HOLD 3-2 SERIES EDGE OVER VEGAS
headline.deck: Game 6 set for Sunday on ABC as Carolina chases second Stanley Cup in franchise history.
headline.body:
RALEIGH — The Carolina Hurricanes have done everything but engrave their names on the Stanley Cup, holding a three-games-to-two series lead over the Vegas Golden Knights with Game 6 scheduled for Sunday night at 8 p.m. ET on ABC. Carolina, which finished the regular season at 53-22-7, enters the game as heavy favorites to claim the second championship in franchise history, and the oddsmakers have anointed center Jordan Staal as the frontrunner for the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP.

Staal's emergence as the series' defining figure has been one of the signature stories of the 2026 postseason. The veteran center, long celebrated for his two-way play and locker room presence, has elevated his game at precisely the right moment, giving the Hurricanes a physical and emotional anchor against a Vegas club that went 39-26-17 in the regular season. The Golden Knights will need to win Sunday to force a Game 7 and keep their championship hopes alive.

The stakes could not be higher for both franchises. Carolina is on the doorstep of a celebration that would validate years of roster building and coaching investment. Vegas, meanwhile, faces elimination on the road with a roster that has shown championship pedigree in recent years. Sunday's game figures to be among the most-watched hockey broadcasts of the season, with the Cup potentially raised before the night is over.

secondary.headline: KNICKS WITHIN ONE WIN OF NBA TITLE; ANUNOBY ODDS CLIMB FOR FINALS MVP
secondary.deck: New York's Game 4 comeback stuns San Antonio and pushes Knicks to the brink of glory.
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Knicks are one victory away from the NBA championship after a shocking comeback win over the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4, a result that has sent the oddsmakers scrambling. New York has been installed as minus-500 favorites to win the title, and forward OG Anunoby has emerged as a leading candidate for the Finals MVP award on the strength of his two-way dominance throughout the series.

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson spent Friday publicly declaring his confidence in guard De'Aaron Fox, whose rough showing in Game 4 left San Antonio searching for answers. Fox will need to rediscover his best basketball if the Spurs are to extend the series in Game 5. The Knicks, meanwhile, need only to stay composed. As Magic Johnson told ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, New York must stay within themselves to play the brand of basketball that has brought them to this moment.

secondary.headline: MARLINS ERUPT FOR FIVE RUNS IN FINAL THREE INNINGS TO ROUT PIRATES, 8-3
secondary.deck: Lowe's 17th home run leads Miami as road win streak continues at PNC Park.
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — The Miami Marlins arrived at PNC Park on Friday night and left with a convincing 8-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates, continuing what has become a reliable road winning streak for a club sitting at .500 on the season. The game was decided in the game's final frames, with Miami scoring four runs in the seventh inning and two more in the eighth to pull away after the Pirates had briefly threatened. Attendance was 19,587 and the game was completed in two hours and 38 minutes.

Nate Lowe launched his 17th home run of the season to pace the Miami offense, while Hicks added his 13th with a double as part of a multi-hit performance, and Rodríguez contributed his second long ball of the year. Pittsburgh managed just three runs, plating one in the third and one in the fifth before adding a final run in the eighth, but the Pirates could never sustain pressure against a Marlins bullpen that shut the door emphatically. Both teams sit at 35-35, making every game in this series carry real weight in the National League standings.

secondary.headline: MARINERS HAMMER NATIONALS, 10-2, BEHIND FOUR HOME RUNS IN WASHINGTON ROUT
secondary.deck: Cornelio earns the win as Seattle sends Washington to another home defeat in lopsided affair.
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON — The Seattle Mariners pounded the Washington Nationals 10-2 on Friday night at Nationals Park, handing Washington another loss in a home losing streak that has become one of the more glaring problems for a club already sitting at 35-35. Seattle scored five times in the second inning to seize control and never looked back, adding three more in the fifth, one in the eighth and one in the ninth. Johzan Orrander Cornelio earned the win for the Mariners, who are atop the AL West at 37-34. The game featured a two-hour, 11-minute delay and was played before 22,226 fans.

The offensive fireworks were abundant. Bo Naylor hit his eighth home run, Dominic Canzone connected for his 10th, Emerson added his fifth, Ryan Wood crushed his 19th, and Jackson Crews contributed his third. The five-homer outburst underscored why Seattle enters Saturday as one of the American League's most dangerous offenses. Washington, dropping to fourth in the NL East, now faces the Mariners again Saturday looking to end the bleeding at home.

column.headline: CAROLINA'S STAAL IS WRITING THE LAST CHAPTER OF A HALL-OF-FAME STORY
column.body:
There is a particular beauty in watching a career come full circle. Jordan Staal has spent years being called a steadying presence, a checking-line anchor, a two-way conscience. Those are compliments wrapped in the language of limitation. Now, with the Conn Smythe Trophy conversation swirling around his name and the Stanley Cup one win away, Staal is forcing everyone to reconsider the ceiling they quietly placed on him years ago. Carolina's 3-2 series lead over Vegas did not happen by accident. It happened because Staal, at this stage of his career, is playing the best hockey of his postseason life.

The Knicks are one win from a championship and the Red Sox throttled Texas by nine runs on Friday night, so there is no shortage of compelling sports theater this weekend. But nothing on the schedule Sunday competes with what happens if Carolina hoists the Cup on home ice. Staal, the franchise cornerstone who has weathered rebuilds and near-misses, would finally have the moment that his career deserved all along. Sometimes the game rewards patience. Sunday night, it just might reward Jordan Staal.

story.headline: METS KNOCK OFF NL EAST-LEADING BRAVES, 7-5, AS SOTO HOMERS IN BATTLE DELAYED BY RAIN
story.deck: New York hands Atlanta another loss despite late Braves rally at Citi Field
story.body:
NEW YORK, June 12 — Juan Soto's 15th home run of the season highlighted a four-run second inning that proved the difference as the New York Mets defeated the first-place Atlanta Braves, 7-5, Friday night at Citi Field, handing the NL East leaders a loss they could ill afford. The game, attended by 38,438 fans and delayed 76 minutes, saw the Mets jump out to a 6-2 lead through four innings before Atlanta mounted a late charge.

The Braves, who entered play at 45-24 and holding the top spot in the NL East, got home runs from Matt Olson — his 20th of the year — and Bo Bichette, his eighth, to keep things interesting. Atlanta scored twice in the eighth inning to pull within 7-5, but the Mets bullpen slammed the door shut in the ninth. Marcus Strider hit Benge with a pitch during the contest, and Riley and Melendez each added doubles for the Braves, who could not convert their late opportunities with 19 runners left on base.

The Mets, sitting fifth in the NL East at 31-38, had little margin for error in the standings but showed no fear against the division's best club. The victory snapped whatever momentum Atlanta carried into the series opener. In other Friday action, the Boston Red Sox routed the Texas Rangers 10-1 behind home runs from Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu and William Contreras, while the Toronto Blue Jays topped the New York Yankees 8-5 at Rogers Centre as Cody Bellinger, George Springer and Masatoshi Okamoto all went deep.

story.headline: KNICKS ONE WIN FROM TITLE AS SPURS COACH BACKS FOX AFTER BRUTAL GAME 4
story.deck: New York reaches -500 odds while San Antonio vows bounce-back in Game 5
story.body:
The New York Knicks stand one victory away from their first NBA championship in more than five decades after a stunning Game 4 comeback pushed them to a 3-1 series lead over the San Antonio Spurs. Oddsmakers have installed the Knicks as massive -500 favorites to close out the series, and OG Anunoby has emerged as a leading contender for Finals MVP honors after a dominant two-way performance that keyed the comeback victory. Magic Johnson, appearing on ESPN, offered the Spurs a sliver of hope, predicting a Game 6 return to Madison Square Garden, but cautioned that New York must stay within themselves to play great basketball and avoid a letdown.

Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson stood firmly behind De'Aaron Fox on Friday, one day after Fox struggled mightily in Game 4. The young guard finished with a forgettable stat line and several costly turnovers as the Knicks' defense swarmed him relentlessly in the fourth quarter. Despite the rough outing, Mitch Johnson told reporters that Fox is his guy and that the organization's belief in him has not wavered heading into a must-win Game 5 in San Antonio.

Off the court, the basketball world absorbed news that the Big3 league, co-founded by rapper Ice Cube, is eyeing a $290 million valuation as it prepares to go public, adding another chapter to the sport's expanding business landscape. But all eyes remain on the Spurs and Knicks, with Game 5 set to tip off Sunday night at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, where a sellout crowd will push Fox and company to force the series back to New York.

story.headline: HURRICANES ONE WIN FROM THE CUP AS STAAL EMERGES AS CONN SMYTHE FAVORITE
story.deck: Carolina carries a 3-2 series lead into Sunday's Game 6 against Vegas.
story.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes are on the doorstep of their second Stanley Cup championship in franchise history, holding a 3-2 series advantage over the Vegas Golden Knights heading into Sunday's Game 6 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and the ESPN App. The Hurricanes, who finished the regular season at a dominant 53-22-7, have been the class of the postseason, and oddsmakers have installed them as heavy favorites to close out the Golden Knights and hoist the Cup in the desert.

At the center of Carolina's surge is Jordan Staal, who has risen to become the new frontrunner for the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. The veteran center has anchored the Hurricanes' two-way game throughout the postseason, providing the kind of physical, relentless play that has worn Vegas down through five brutal games. The Golden Knights, who limped through the regular season at just 39-26-17, have relied on grit and goaltending to push this series to the brink, but time is running out.

Former NHL defenseman P.K. Subban did not mince words when assessing Vegas's situation, saying the Golden Knights need to 'buckle up' if they hope to force a Game 7 back in Carolina. Vegas will need a complete effort from their forwards and a standout performance in goal to survive Sunday night. For the Hurricanes, one more win delivers a championship to Raleigh for just the second time since the franchise relocated from Hartford in 1997.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are betting big on new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-scale quarterback revolution, with front offices across the league making aggressive moves to secure their franchises at the most critical position on the field. The Las Vegas Raiders, still searching for stability under center after years of disappointment, agreed to terms with veteran QB Sam Darnold on a two-year, $54 million deal, banking on his resurgent 2025 campaign to carry a retooled offense into the fall. Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers traded up to select Toledo's electrifying dual-threat prospect Marcus Webb with the fifth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, ending months of speculation about the direction of the rebuild.

The draft itself produced several headline moments beyond Carolina's bold move. The Cleveland Browns, working with new offensive coordinator Dana Stubbs, grabbed Alabama wide receiver Darius Fontaine in the first round to give young quarterback Caleb Williams a genuine deep threat after acquiring Williams in a blockbuster March trade with Chicago. The Bears, gutted after moving their former top pick, responded by stockpiling four picks in the first two rounds, signaling general manager Ryan Poles is committed to another full reconstruction of the roster from the ground up.

On the free agency front, left tackle Laremy Tunsil inked a surprise one-year deal with the Dallas Cowboys after the Houston Texans declined to match the offer, instantly upgrading a Dallas offensive line that surrendered 52 sacks last season. The New England Patriots, now in their third year under head coach Mike Vrabel, also made noise by signing linebacker Roquan Smith away from the Baltimore Ravens, adding a proven defensive anchor as Vrabel pushes to return New England to playoff contention for the first time since Super Bowl LX runner-up Kansas City's grip on the AFC loosened.
